elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 13 retains automatic renewal ("shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods"), so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be met; the 60-day reminder and CPI/3% cap are absent, so the mutual-agreement gateway is not satisfied.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 13: renewal is for "successive one year periods" — each renewal term is 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13 already permits either party to give "written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year"; the inserted sentence restates the same 30-day window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder covenant appears anywhere in the rendered Sections 6 or 13 or in the inserted sentence; the drafter expressly declines to press it. Repair requires an operative TrueLink obligation to notify Client at least 60 days before each renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence caps increases at "five percent (5%) in any renewal term" — a 5% flat cap, not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 13 as retained requires non-renewal notice "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year", and the inserted sentence confirms "no more than thirty (30) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — 30 days, inside the 60-day ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a regex miss; the numeral 30 is present in both the retained and inserted text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term." This closes the gap left by Section 6, which freezes Hosting Services costs only "for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement".

reasons: Fallback level is position-complete: the retained Section 13 30-day non-renewal window already satisfies the ≤60-day element, and the inserted 5% cap satisfies the price-increase element, which was otherwise uncapped after the Section 6 first-year freeze expires.
Preferred level fails on two elements: there is no Vendor reminder obligation 60 days before renewal, and the cap is a flat 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%.

Minimality fails: the first half of the inserted sentence re-states a term the contract already contains. Section 13 already provides non-renewal notice "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year", so the fallback notice-window element required no edit at all. Restating it creates duplicate operative language on the same commercial term (and a second, differently worded formulation — "no more than thirty (30) days" versus "no later than thirty (30) days") that a counterparty could read as an independent covenant. Delete the notice-window clause from the insertion and let the edit read only: "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term."

Intent is preserved: the Section 6 one-year freeze and most-favoured-rate covenant, the Section 12 termination cross-reference, and the 30/60-day discontinuation mechanics all survive without contradiction, and the cap is expressly limited to "any renewal term" so it does not collide with the first-year freeze.

Note on scope: the cap reaches "TrueLink's fees" generally rather than only Hosting Services fees. That is broader than the retained Section 6 freeze but operates in Client's favour and within the renewal-pricing element, so it is not treated as an out-of-checklist addition.
